options.text: "Pivot the Palace's public schedule entirely back to domestic economic recovery and the upcoming MPR session, declining all further press questions on East Timor."
options.reaction:
POS KOTA: 'TIMTIM LEPAS, ISTANA PURA-PURA PIKUN!'

As foreign tanks roll through Dili, a city built over twenty-four years with trillions of rupiah in Indonesian tax money and the lives of thousands of soldiers, President Habibie's press office announced yesterday that the Palace has 'moved on' to domestic economic agendas and will take no further questions on East Timor. Cartoonists in this morning's papers depicted the President whistling past a graveyard with his fingers plugged firmly in his ears, while MPR faction leaders promised that East Timor will be Question Number One when he steps to the podium on October 14.

title: Semanggi II Tragedy
desc: Yesterday afternoon, in its final days before dissolving, the outgoing DPR rushed through the State of Danger Bill (RUU Penanggulangan Keadaan Bahaya / PKB), a sweeping statute championed by Defense Minister General Wiranto to replace the 1959 emergency law, granting the President and regional military commanders broad powers to declare states of civil or military emergency, ban demonstrations, wiretap communications, and detain suspects. Seeing the bill as the reincarnation of New Order authoritarianism, tens of thousands of university students from UI, Trisakti, and Atma Jaya have occupied Jalan Gatot Subroto and the Semanggi cloverleaf outside the DPR/MPR complex. Over the past twenty-four hours, security forces have fired tear gas and live rounds into the crowds: University of Indonesia engineering student Yap Yun Hap has been shot dead near Semanggi, and violent clashes in Jakarta, Lampung, and Palembang have left eleven dead and over two hundred wounded. With the MPR convening in seven days, the capital is on the verge of exploding.

options.text: "Refuse to sign the State of Danger Bill (RUU PKB) into law and announce an indefinite postponement of its ratification, depriving the bill of legal force and immediately pulling the fuse out of the student uprising before the MPR convenes."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'SETELAH NYAWA YAP YUN HAP MELAYANG, BARU ISTANA TUNDA UU PENANGGULANGAN KEADAAN BAHAYA'

Why does it always take student corpses on the asphalt of Jalan Sudirman before the Habibie government listens to its own people? That was the bitter question asked by University of Indonesia students weeping over the casket of engineering student Yap Yun Hap at the UI Salemba campus yesterday, hours after the Palace announced it was shelving the hated State of Danger Bill (RUU PKB). While freezing the bill prevented a full-scale insurrection ahead of next week's MPR session, student senates pointed out that Habibie's own ministers drafted and pushed the draconian bill through the DPR in the first place, and inside Cilangkap, General Wiranto's staff are furious at being abandoned mid-stream.

options.text: "Postpone the Security Bill AND order Jakarta Military Commander Maj. Gen. Djaja Suparman and National Police Chief Gen. Roesmanhadi to identify and court-martial the personnel who fired live rounds at Yap Yun Hap and the protesters."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'TUMBAL DI JEMBATAN SEMANGGI: PRAJURIT BAWAHAN DIKORBANKAN, PEMBERI KOMANDO AMAN'

Shelving the RUU PKB and ordering Military Police to arrest the field personnel who fired live ammunition at Semanggi II has cooled the barricades along Jalan Gatot Subroto, but neither the students nor the officer corps are satisfied. At UI Salemba, student leaders noted that the shooters from Trisakti (May 1998) and Semanggi I (November 1998) were similarly 'investigated' while the generals who deployed combat troops with live rounds went untouched; meanwhile, Kodam Jaya and Brimob commanders are fuming that the Palace pushed their men onto the streets to defend a government bill and then threw them to the wolves when bullets flew.

options.text: "Receive a delegation of UI rectorate leaders and student representatives at Merdeka Palace to express condolences to Yap Yun Hap's family and form a joint civilian-student review team on the emergency law."
options.reaction:
RAKYAT MERDEKA: 'MAHASISWA DITEMBAK PELURU TAJAM, HABIBIE MALAH AJAK BIKIN TIM KAJIAN!'

With eleven protesters dead across Jakarta, Lampung, and Palembang and over two hundred students lying in hospital wards at St. Carolus and Atma Jaya with gunshot wounds and shattered skulls, Merdeka Palace's offer to form a 'joint academic review team' on the State Security Bill was greeted with derision on the streets. Student coalitions from FORKOT, FAMRED, and KB-UI boycotted the Palace invitation outright, burning copies of the RUU PKB at the Semanggi flyover and chanting that they want the law dead, not edited.

options.text: "Deliver an unscripted televised address offering personal prayers for the victims at Semanggi and Lampung while pleading with students to return to their campuses so the MPR General Session can proceed in peace."
options.reaction:
POS KOTA: 'AIR MATA BUAYA DI LAYAR KACA TAK BISA HIDUPKAN KEMBALI YAP YUN HAP!'

President Habibie's emotional, rambling television address last night, pleading for calm while refusing to explicitly kill the State of Danger Bill that sparked the bloodshed, landed with a thud across the capital. Tens of thousands of mourners marching behind Yap Yun Hap's hearse from Salemba to Tanah Kusir jeered the President's name, pointing out that less than eleven months after Semanggi I, security forces under his command have once again gunned unarmed students down on the exact same stretch of asphalt.

options.text: "Sign the State of Danger Bill (UU PKB) into law immediately and authorize Maj. Gen. Djaja Suparman to invoke its emergency provisions to clear Jalan Gatot Subroto before the MPR delegates arrive on October 1."
options.reaction:
MEDIA INDONESIA: 'JAKARTA DARURAT PERANG: HABIBIE TEKEN UU PKB DI ATAS DARAH MAHASISWA SEMANGGI'

By signing the despised State of Danger Bill into law on the very day University of Indonesia student Yap Yun Hap was buried, President Habibie has severed his last thread of democratic legitimacy. Over the past twelve hours, central Jakarta has descended into open urban warfare: black smoke billows from burning police posts along Jalan Sudirman, campuses in Yogyakarta, Bandung, and Surabaya have declared a nationwide strike, and Amien Rais warned from Senayan that the President has handed his opponents the ultimate reason to reject his Accountability Speech.

title: PwC Bank Bali Audit Leaks
desc: Three days before the new MPR is sworn in, the complete 120-page PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) long-form forensic audit of the Bank Bali scandal has leaked in full to DPR Commission VIII and the Jakarta press corps. Although Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) Chairman Billy Joedono initially distributed only a sanitized 41-page summary omitting individual names on bank-secrecy grounds, the leaked unredacted PwC report names everyone: it documents indicators of fraud, collusion, and political interference tracing the Rp 546 billion from Bank Bali through Djoko Tjandra and Setya Novanto's PT Era Giat Prima straight to accounts linked to DPA Chairman A.A. Baramuli, State Enterprises Minister Tanri Abeng, IBRA officials, BI Governor Sjahril Sabirin, and your own 'Tim Sukses' re-election operation. DPR Pansus members are holding up copies of the leaked pages for television cameras in Senayan.

options.text: "Declassify and transmit the full unredacted 120-page PwC audit to the DPR Pansus committee, and instruct the Attorney General and National Police to question every official named in it, including A.A. Baramuli and Setya Novanto."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'AUDIT PWC BUKA BOROK TIM SUKSES: HABIBIE LEMPAR BARAMULI KE KANDANG SINGA DPR'

Only after photocopies of the unredacted 120-page PricewaterhouseCoopers forensic audit were already circulating in every newsroom and embassy in Jakarta did Merdeka Palace finally bow to reality and 'declassify' the report. And what a devastating document it is: page after page traces the Rp 546 billion Bank Bali payout through Setya Novanto and Djoko Tjandra's PT Era Giat Prima straight into the inner sanctum of Habibie's own re-election machine (Tim Sukses). Inside Golkar, a furious A.A. Baramuli is threatening to drag down everyone with him if prosecuted, while Akbar Tandjung's camp is openly preparing to abandon a presidency drowning in sleaze.

options.text: "Stand behind BPK Chairman Billy Joedono's statutory interpretation: release the 41-page official summary publicly while keeping the raw annexes restricted to law enforcement investigators under Indonesia's banking secrecy statute."
options.reaction:
RAKYAT MERDEKA: 'SENSOR SPIDOL HITAM BPK JADI BAHAN TERTAWAAN! FOTOKOPI AUDIT PWC DIJUAL DI LAMPU MERAH'

Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) Chairman Billy Joedono and Bina Graha turned themselves into a national laughingstock yesterday by solemnly handing DPR members a sanitized 41-page 'summary' of the PwC Bank Bali report with all the politicians' names scrubbed out, at the exact moment street boys at the Kuningan and Slipi traffic lights were hawking bootleg copies of the full 120-page unredacted audit for Rp 10,000 apiece! 'The Palace is trying to hide an elephant behind a handkerchief,' DPR Pansus member Angelina Sondakh's colleagues jeered on the floor.

options.text: "Call on Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin and IBRA Chairman Glenn Yusuf to accept institutional responsibility for the regulatory failure that allowed the Rp 904 billion interbank claim to be paid out in the first place."
options.reaction:
BISNIS INDONESIA: 'DITUDING ISTANA, GUBERNUR BI SJAHRIL SABIRIN MELAWAN DAN BONGKAR TEKANAN BARAMULI'

President Habibie's attempt to pin the blame for the Bank Bali scandal on Bank Indonesia Governor Sjahril Sabirin and IBRA Chairman Glenn Yusuf backfired spectacularly in DPR hearings yesterday afternoon. Protected by the central bank independence statute Habibie himself signed in May, Sabirin flatly refused to resign and instead testified under oath that he only authorized the Rp 904 billion transfer after relentless political pressure and threats from Habibie's closest confidant, DPA Chairman A.A. Baramuli.

options.text: "Have State Enterprises Minister Tanri Abeng and your legal counsel argue that since the Rp 546 billion has now been frozen in escrow at Bank Indonesia, the state treasury has suffered zero net financial loss."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'LOGIKA ABSURD TANPA KERUGIAN NEGARA: PENJARAHAN BANK BALI BUKAN SEKADAR SOAL AKUNTANSI'

The Palace's latest legal defense of the Bank Bali scandal, claiming that because the Rp 546 billion was eventually frozen in escrow, 'the state suffered zero loss and therefore no corruption occurred', was shredded by legal scholars and IMF officials alike yesterday. 'By that logic, a bank robber who drops the money bag when surrounded by police at the door commits no crime,' banking analyst Pradjoto told Kompas, noting that the PwC audit proves beyond doubt a premeditated conspiracy to loot state recapitalization funds for the October presidential election.

options.text: "Declare the leaked PwC document a violation of state and banking secrecy laws, and order the police to raid the offices of the newspapers and DPR staffers circulating the unredacted pages."
options.reaction:
THE JAKARTA POST: 'POLICE RAID DPR OFFICES OVER PWC LEAK AS IMF CONDEMNS COVER-UP'

In a breathtaking act of political self-destruction just seventy-two hours before the MPR convenes, the Habibie government has sent police investigators into Senayan to hunt down the leakers of the 120-page PwC Bank Bali audit rather than the thieves named inside it. In response, student protesters plastered enlarged pages of the audit showing the transfers to Setya Novanto and Baramuli's network across the walls of the DPR compound, while IMF Director Hubert Neiss announced from Washington that Indonesia's bailout remains frozen solid.

title: MPR Convenes
desc: All 700 delegates of the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR), 462 elected DPR party representatives, 38 appointed ABRI officers, 135 provincial delegates (Utusan Daerah) elected by the 27 regional parliaments, and 65 civic and functional delegates (Utusan Golongan), have taken their oaths beneath the green tortoiseshell dome of the Senayan complex. Before your Accountability Speech or the presidential election can take place, the Assembly must elect two crucial leaders: the Speaker of the MPR (who will preside over the General Session and set the rules for your Accountability Vote) on October 3, and the Speaker of the DPR on October 6. In the hotel suites of the Hilton and the Mulia, a high-stakes three-way chess match is underway between Amien Rais, PKB Chairman Matori Abdul Djalil (backed by Megawati's PDI-P), and Golkar Chairman Akbar Tandjung.

options.text: "Execute a grand parliamentary bargain: instruct Golkar's whips to back Amien Rais for MPR Speaker against PDI-P's candidate Matori Abdul Djalil on October 3, in exchange for the Islamic parties backing Akbar Tandjung for DPR Speaker on October 6."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'AMIEN RAIS KETUA MPR, AKBAR TANDJUNG KETUA DPR: KEMENANGAN TAKTIS YANG MENYIMPAN RANJAU BAGI HABIBIE'

On paper, the hotel-suite pact engineered between Golkar and the Islamic parties was a surgical triumph, electing Amien Rais as MPR Speaker (305–279 over PDI-P's Matori Abdul Djalil) and handing Akbar Tandjung the DPR Speakership by a landslide (411 votes). Yet seasoned Senayan veterans are asking whether President Habibie just built the gallows for his own presidency: Amien Rais now holds the MPR gavel to advance his own 'Central Axis' candidate, and Akbar Tandjung has already secured the five-year prize he wanted most, leaving him with zero incentive to go down with Habibie's sinking ship on October 19.

options.text: "Throw the Palace's full weight behind Akbar Tandjung for the DPR Speakership unconditionally, rallying both Golkar wings and the regional delegates to demonstrate the Banyan Tree's discipline."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'AKBAR TANDJUNG AMANKAN KURSI KETUA DPR, HABIBIE BELUM TENTU KEBAGIAN KURSI PRESIDEN'

With Palace whips delivering the regional and Golkar blocs en masse, Akbar Tandjung coasted to the DPR Speakership yesterday with 411 votes. But inside the Hilton Hotel suites where Akbar's former HMI (Islamic Students Association) lieutenants gather late at night, the mood was anything but grateful toward Merdeka Palace. 'Habibie paid cash up front to make Akbar the second most powerful man in the country, and now Akbar holds all the cards for the next two weeks,' observed political analyst Eep Saefulloh Fatah.

options.text: "Reach across the aisle to Diponegoro: offer Golkar support for PDI-P's preferred leadership slate in the DPR and MPR in exchange for PDI-P toning down its attacks on your upcoming Accountability Speech."
options.reaction:
SUARA KARYA: 'MANUVER ISTANA DEKATI PDI-P PICU PEMBERONTAKAN FRAKSI GOLKAR DI SENAYAN'

President Habibie's backchannel offer to trade away Golkar's claim on the parliamentary leadership in exchange for a softer PDI-P stance on his Accountability Speech triggered an open mutiny inside his own party caucus yesterday. Defying Bina Graha's emissaries outright, Akbar Tandjung's 120 DPR legislators cut their own deal with Amien Rais and ABRI to seize the Speakerships anyway, leaving Habibie alienated from his own party apparatus while PDI-P pockets his concessions with a smirk.

options.text: "Host the 135 Utusan Daerah and 65 Utusan Golongan delegates at Istana Negara to organize an independent non-partisan 'Fraksi Utusan' bloc loyal directly to the Presidency."
options.reaction:
RAKYAT MERDEKA: 'JAMUAN KAVIAR DI ISTANA GAGAL! DPR BUBARKAN FRAKSI UTUSAN DAERAH ANDALAN HABIBIE'

After wining and dining 200 regional and functional delegates at Istana Negara in a blatant attempt to reconstruct Suharto's old 200-vote rubber-stamp Fraksi Utusan Daerah, Bina Graha suffered a humiliating defeat on the MPR floor yesterday afternoon. United for once in their determination to stop the Palace from herding regional delegates like cattle, PDI-P, PKB, PAN, and even Akbar Tandjung's Golkar voted to abolish the standalone Regional Faction, forcing provincial delegates to sit inside the regular party caucuses!

options.text: "Respect the separation of powers strictly: keep Merdeka Palace out of the parliamentary Speakership elections and let the 700 delegates choose their own presiding officers."
options.reaction:
MEDIA INDONESIA: 'HABIBIE JADI PENONTON DI SENAYAN SAAT AMIEN RAIS DAN AKBAR BAGI-BAGI KEKUASAAN'

While Amien Rais, Akbar Tandjung, Taufik Kiemas, and General Wiranto spent the last seventy-two hours locked in marathon horse-trading across the hotel suites of central Jakarta to divide the MPR and DPR Speakerships, Merdeka Palace sat on its hands piously preaching 'separation of powers.' The result is a parliamentary leadership that owes its gavels entirely to its own backroom deals and nothing whatsoever to B.J. Habibie.

title: The Central Axis Nominates Gus Dur
desc:
Fresh off his election as MPR Speaker on October 3, Amien Rais has pulled off a political masterstroke that has shattered the two-horse race between you and Megawati Sukarnoputri. At a packed press conference today, flanked by leaders of the Reform Faction (PAN and PK), PPP Chairman Hamzah Haz, PKB Chairman Matori Abdul Djalil, and PBB Chairman Yusril Ihza Mahendra, the newly consolidated 'Poros Tengah' (Central Axis) has formally nominated Abdurrahman Wahid (Gus Dur, the near-blind cleric who leads the 40-million-strong Nahdlatul Ulama) as its candidate for President of the Republic. While Gus Dur himself had previously expressed sympathy for Megawati, he has accepted the nomination to prevent what the ulama call a destructive polarization between secular nationalists and political Islam.

Amien Rais has formally consolidated the Islamic parties, absorbing PPP, PKB, and 20 minor Islamic party delegates into the 'Poros Tengah' coalition. Instantly commanding 163 MPR Delegates and transforming into the ultimate kingmaker of the General Session.

options.text: "Welcome Gus Dur's nomination graciously as proof of Indonesia's democratic maturity, while reminding the Central Axis that splitting the Muslim and reformist vote risks handing the presidency straight to PDI-P unless we coordinate on the Accountability Vote first."
options.reaction:
REPUBLIKA: 'HABIBIE SAMBUT PENCALONAN GUS DUR, TAPI POROS TENGAH SIAPKAN SKENARIO TANPA HABIBIE'

President Habibie's polite welcome for Abdurrahman Wahid's surprise presidential nomination could not mask the cold sweat breaking out inside his campaign headquarters at Patra Kuningan. For months, Habibie's strategists had assumed the Islamic parties would have no choice but to back the founder of ICMI in order to stop Megawati. Now, by nominating Gus Dur, Amien Rais has given Muslim and reformist delegates a viable third door; one that only opens wide if Habibie's Accountability Speech is voted down on October 19.

options.text: "Meet privately with Gus Dur and Amien Rais to propose a grand power-sharing ticket: support your re-election as President on October 20 with Gus Dur or Hamzah Haz elevated to a constitutionally empowered Vice Presidency."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'DITAWARI KURSI WAPRES OLEH HABIBIE, GUS DUR BERSeloroh: NGAPAIN JADI WAKIL KALAU BISA JADI PRESIDEN?'

Abdurrahman Wahid needed only one sentence to puncture Bina Graha's latest trial balloon yesterday afternoon. Asked by reporters outside the Ciganjur compound about President Habibie's offer to make him or Hamzah Haz Vice President in exchange for Poros Tengah's 163 votes, the near-blind NU cleric chuckled: 'Why on earth should I apply to be Pak Habibie's assistant when Amien Rais is already working overtime to make me his replacement?' The press corps roared with laughter, though PPP insiders privately admit they are still listening to Palace offers.

options.text: "Bypass Amien Rais and send an emergency envoy to Megawati Sukarnoputri and Taufik Kiemas: propose a nationalist-technocratic understanding between Golkar and PDI-P to stop Amien Rais's Central Axis from hijacking the election."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'PANIK DIKEPUNG POROS TENGAH, ISTANA COBA MERAYU BANTENG YANG TERLUKA'

Politics makes strange bedfellows, but watching B.J. Habibie's emissaries knock on Jalan Diponegoro's door to warn Megawati Sukarnoputri about Amien Rais's 'treachery' takes the prize for 1999. While Taufik Kiemas's pragmatic wing inside PDI-P is furious at Gus Dur for abandoning his alliance with Megawati and heard the Palace envoy out, PDI-P's rank-and-file delegates remain adamant that they will never vote to accept Habibie's Accountability Speech just to spite Amien Rais.

options.text: "Double down on the Banyan Tree and the provinces: ignore the Central Axis's maneuvering and concentrate all Palace resources on locking down Golkar's 120 DPR seats, ABRI's 38 seats, and the 135 Utusan Daerah delegates."
options.reaction:
THE JAKARTA POST: 'PALACE DISMISSES CENTRAL AXIS AS BLUFF, BETS THE HOUSE ON GOLKAR AND REGIONAL VOTES'

Campaign strategists inside Habibie's Tim Sukses dismissed Gus Dur's nomination by the Central Axis yesterday as 'a paper tiger that will fold before October 20,' vowing instead to steamroll the MPR with Golkar, ABRI, and outer-island delegates. Parliamentary mathematicians in Senayan were less impressed: with PPP, PKB, and PAN now consolidated into a 163-seat bloc under Speaker Amien Rais, snubbing the Central Axis leaves Habibie with zero margin for error if even thirty Golkar delegates defect behind the secret-ballot curtain.

options.text: "Have Palace surrogates publicly question whether a man who has suffered two near-fatal strokes and cannot read a briefing paper with his own eyes is medically fit under Article 6 of the Constitution to serve as President."
options.reaction:
RAKYAT MERDEKA: 'HINA FISIK GUS DUR, JUTAAN WARGA NAHDLIYIN DAN BANSER NGAMUK KE ISTANA!'

Of all the blunders committed by President Habibie's surrogates this year, publicly mocking Abdurrahman Wahid's blindness and stroke recovery as a constitutional disqualification under Article 6 may prove the most suicidal. Within hours, Nahdlatul Ulama boarding schools across East and Central Java erupted in fury, Banser youth brigades burned Habibie campaign banners in Surabaya and Jombang, and wavering PKB and PPP delegates vowed to bury the President's Accountability Speech on October 19.

title: Suharto SP3 Order
desc: Three days before you are scheduled to step to the MPR podium to deliver your Accountability Speech, Acting Attorney General Ismudjoko, who replaced Lt. Gen. Andi Muhammad Ghalib in June after Indonesia Corruption Watch (ICW) exposed suspicious bank transfers and a leaked wiretap of your private phone call to Ghalib ('Halo Andi...') mocked the anti-corruption probe, has dropped a political grenade. Today, October 11, Ismudjoko formally issued an SP3 (Surat Perintah Penghentian Penyidikan / Order to Terminate Investigation) shutting down the state corruption investigation into former President Suharto and his seven charitable foundations (Dakab, Supersemar, Dharmais), citing 'insufficient legal evidence of state losses' and Suharto's recent hospitalization at Pertamina Central Hospital. Within hours of the announcement, thousands of furious students have marched toward Jalan Cendana and the Attorney General's Office in Blok M, chanting that your entire 17-month presidency was a calculated charade to pardon your old mentor.

options.text: "Override Acting Attorney General Ismudjoko immediately: annul the SP3 order, place Suharto's seven foundation accounts under full state receivership, and pledge before the MPR that the corruption probe will continue under an independent special prosecutor."
options.reaction:
MEDIA INDONESIA: 'PANIK DIKEPUNG MAHASISWA, HABIBIE BATALKAN SP3 SOEHARTO H-3 PIDATO PERTANGGUNGJAWABAN'

Terrified that Acting Attorney General Ismudjoko's October 11 termination of the Suharto corruption probe would ignite a student revolution on the eve of his Accountability Speech, President Habibie scrambled yesterday to annul the SP3 order and seize the Cendana foundations. While anti-corruption activists welcomed the reversal, nobody in Senayan missed the opportunism of the timing: for sixteen months Habibie slow-walked the probe, even getting caught on a wiretap coaching Andi Ghalib, only to discover anti-Suharto zeal seventy-two hours before the MPR votes on his job. Meanwhile, Jalan Cendana's financiers have declared total war on Habibie's candidacy.

options.text: "Uphold the Attorney General's SP3 order on legal and humanitarian grounds, reminding the nation that Suharto has already transferred Rp 4 trillion in foundation assets to the state under Keppres No. 133/1998 and is gravely ill."
options.reaction:
RAKYAT MERDEKA: 'MURID BAKTI PADA SANG GURU! HABIBIE RESMIKAN SP3 SOEHARTO, REFORMASI DIKHIANATI'

The charade that began with the leaked 'Halo, Andi? Apa kabar?' wiretap in February reached its cynical climax yesterday afternoon as Acting Attorney General Ismudjoko, with President Habibie's full blessing, issued an SP3 order dropping all corruption charges against former President Suharto just three days before the MPR Accountability Speech! Molotov cocktails rained down on the gates of the Attorney General's Office in Blok M last night as thousands of students clashed with riot police, chanting that the man who once called Suharto 'Super Genius' was installed in May 1998 for one purpose only: to wash his master's sins clean.

options.text: "Clarify through Justice Minister Muladi that an SP3 is only a provisional suspension while Suharto is hospitalized at Pertamina Hospital, and sign an instruction keeping the travel ban on Tommy Suharto and the Cendana family strictly in force."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'AKROBAT HUKUM MULADI: SP3 DISEBUT SEMENTARA, SOEHARTO TETAP LENGGANG KANGKUNG'

Justice Minister Muladi spent two hours yesterday trying to convince a skeptical press corps that terminating the Suharto corruption investigation via an SP3 on October 11 is merely a 'reversible procedural pause' while the former strongman rests at Pertamina Central Hospital. Legal Aid Foundation (YLBHI) chairman Bambang Widjojanto called the explanation 'insulting legal gymnastics designed to placate Cendana cronies inside Golkar while anesthetizing the students until next week's MPR vote is over.'

options.text: "Insist on strict judicial non-interference: state that under a rule-of-law republic the President cannot order the Attorney General to indict or drop charges against any citizen, and leave the SP3 to judicial pre-trial review."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'MENDADAK HORMATI INDEPENDENSI KEJAKSAAN SETELAH REKAMAN TELEPON ANDI GHALIB'

President Habibie's pious claim yesterday that he 'cannot interfere with the independent legal judgment of Acting Attorney General Ismudjoko' on the Suharto SP3 was greeted with derisive laughter across Senayan. Every newspaper reader in Indonesia still remembers the verbatim transcript of Habibie's private telephone call to former Attorney General Andi Ghalib earlier this year, in which the President choreographed the three-hour questioning of Suharto down to the minute. Pretending to be a bystander now fools not a single soul.

options.text: "Order security forces to place Jalan Cendana under visible 24-hour protective custody and freeze the remaining Supersemar and Dakab foundation disbursements pending an MPR special committee review."
options.reaction:
POS KOTA: 'SANDIWARA JAGA JALAN CENDANA: TENTARA SENYUM HORMAT SAAT MOBIL KELUARGA CENDANA LEWAT!'

To deflect public outrage over the Attorney General's SP3 order dropping the Suharto probe, Bina Graha announced yesterday that soldiers have been posted around No. 8 Jalan Cendana and the family's foundation accounts frozen for MPR review. Pos Kota photographers stationed on Jalan Cendana all afternoon observed a rather different reality: the guards snapped to attention and saluted every time Tutut and Bambang Trihatmodjo's tinted Mercedes convoys glided in and out of the compound.

title: Barricades at Senayan
desc: Tomorrow night you will stand before the 700 delegates of the MPR to deliver your Pidato Pertanggungjawaban. Outside the Senayan parliamentary complex, the atmosphere has reached a boiling point: over a hundred thousand PDI-P supporters, wearing red headbands and waving Banteng flags, have converged with student coalitions along Jalan Gatot Subroto, pressing against massive coils of razor wire, water cannons, and 30,000 Kostrad, Marines, and Brimob troops deployed by General Wiranto. Meanwhile, inside your own camp at Patra Kuningan, your strategists are urging a bold preemptive move before tomorrow night's speech: formally announce General Wiranto as your running mate for Vice President on the 1999–2004 ticket, locking in ABRI's 38 seats and forcing Golkar's wavering nationalist wing under Akbar Tandjung to stay in line.

options.text: "Announce publicly that you have asked General Wiranto to stand as your Vice Presidential running mate for 1999–2004, while instructing the Marines, whom the students respect, to man the front lines at Senayan without live ammunition."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'LAMARAN TERBUKA HABIBIE KEPADA WIRANTO: MANUVER PUTUS ASA ATAU TIKET PENYELAMAT?'

On the eve of his Accountability Speech, President Habibie has played his final trump card by publicly proposing Armed Forces Commander General Wiranto as his Vice Presidential running mate for 1999–2004. Yet while deploying the pink-bereted Marines eased tensions with students along Jalan Gatot Subroto, Wiranto's own response to the marriage proposal was conspicuously frigid: rather than accepting on the spot, the general told reporters he 'needs to consult the officer corps and weigh the national interest first', leaving Habibie hanging in public view like an anxious suitor.

options.text: "Send a personal emissary to Megawati Sukarnoputri and Taufik Kiemas tonight: pledge a clean, democratic vote in the MPR without military intimidation, and offer PDI-P a co-governing coalition if your Accountability Speech is accepted."
options.reaction:
SUARA PEMBARUAN: 'UTUSAN MALAM ISTANA KE KEBAGUSAN: MEGAWATI TENANGKAN MASSA, TAPI TOLAK KOMPROMI PIDATO'

After a late-night visit from Palace emissaries promising an unrigged MPR ballot and dangling a power-sharing cabinet, PDI-P Chairwoman Megawati Sukarnoputri instructed her red-shirted Satgas commanders outside Senayan to pull back from the razor wire and avoid clashes with the Marines. Inside the chamber, however, PDI-P faction leader Dimyati Hartono made clear that peaceful streets will not buy Habibie a single pardon on the floor tomorrow night: 'We will keep our supporters calm outside so the world can watch us reject his speech cleanly inside.'

options.text: "Go on national television and radio tonight to address the students and citizens outside Senayan directly, reminding them that you are standing before the MPR tomorrow under truly democratic rules for the first time in 44 years."
options.reaction:
THE JAKARTA POST: 'HABIBIE PLEADS FOR FAIR HEARING AS 100,000 PROTESTERS RING SENAYAN'

Speaking directly into the television cameras last night, President Habibie reminded the nation that tomorrow night's Pidato Pertanggungjawaban marks the first time since 1955 that an Indonesian head of state will stand before an unscripted parliament that actually has the power to fire him. While civic intellectuals acknowledged the democratic milestone, the sea of red-shirted Banteng supporters and student marchers camped around the Senayan Hilton drowned out the broadcast on giant outdoor screens with deafening chants of 'Tolak! Tolak! Tolak!'

options.text: "Move executive cabinet operations temporarily to Bogor Palace for security continuity while General Wiranto's security ring seals off central Jakarta."
options.reaction:
RAKYAT MERDEKA: 'BELUM DISIDANG SUDAH NGUNGSI KE BOGOR! NYALI ISTANA CIUT LIHAT LAUTAN MERAH DI SENAYAN'

Nothing signals a collapsing regime faster than moving the furniture out of the capital. Word that Bina Graha quietly shifted executive secretariat operations fifty kilometers south to Bogor Palace yesterday as 100,000 PDI-P supporters and students surrounded Senayan triggered immediate mockery across the MPR floor. 'Sukarno went to Bogor in March 1966 right before Supersemar, and Suharto wanted to go to Bogor in May 1998; now Habibie is following the exact same exit map,' one Golkar dissident whispered to reporters at the Hotel Mulia.

options.text: "Order Kodam Jaya and Brimob to clear Jalan Gatot Subroto and the Semanggi approaches by force tonight so MPR delegates do not have to pass a single red flag tomorrow morning."
options.reaction:
POS KOTA: 'SENAYAN BANJIR DARAH DAN GAS AIR MATA H-1 PIDATO HABIBIE!'

Central Jakarta looked like a war zone at dawn today after Brimob riot squads and armored water cannons stormed student and PDI-P encampments along Jalan Gatot Subroto and the Semanggi flyover on orders from the Palace. Over a hundred bloodied demonstrators were carried into Atma Jaya and Jakarta Hospital as tear-gas canisters detonated inside the Hilton Hotel compound where MPR delegates are sleeping, ensuring that when President Habibie walks into the Plenary Hall tonight, the chamber will be waiting for him with pure venom.

title: Pidato Pertanggungjawaban
desc:
Just after nightfall on October 14, 1999, you walk to the rostrum of the Plenary Hall of the People's Consultative Assembly as MPR Speaker Amien Rais bangs the gavel for order. Before you sit 700 delegates, and tens of millions of Indonesians watching live on television, for your Pidato Pertanggungjawaban, the constitutional accounting of your 512 days in office. Unlike the choreographed unanimous ovations of Suharto's six terms, you are greeted by a chorus of 'Huuuu!' jeers and floor interruptions from PDI-P and student-aligned delegates before you even read your first page.

For nearly three hours, and again in your formal reply (Jawaban Presiden) after all eleven MPR factions deliver their sharp critiques over October 15–17, you must frame the overarching narrative of your presidency. Will you anchor your defense in the macroeconomic miracle of rescuing the rupiah from Rp 16,800 to the 7,000s and crushing inflation from 77% to 2%? Will you champion the democratic revolution of freeing political prisoners, unleashing a free press, enacting regional autonomy, and holding the June 1999 election? Or will you confront your two greatest vulnerabilities, East Timor and Bank Bali, head-on?

Your speech tonight grants an immediate burst of Political Capital and sets the tone for the final forty-eight hours of backroom caucuses (Turns 21–22), where all Final Faction Appeals are now unlocked before the October 19 roll call.

options.text: "Lead with the undeniable record of Reformasi and macroeconomic rescue: remind the Assembly that in 512 days we brought the rupiah back from Rp 16,800, broke inflation from 77%, freed political prisoners, enacted Laws No. 22 & 25 on Regional Autonomy, liberated the press, and delivered the freest election since 1955."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'TIGA JAM DI PODIUM MPR: ANGKA STATISTIK HABIBIE DIHADANG HUJATAN TIMTIM DAN BANK BALI'

Standing for nearly three hours beneath the glare of the television lights as PDI-P delegates repeatedly interrupted him with cries of 'Huuuu!', President Habibie marshaled a barrage of macroeconomic charts and legislative statistics, reminding the 700 delegates that his 512-day administration passed 39 laws, cut inflation from 77 percent to single digits, and brought the dollar down from Rp 16,800. Yet when the eleven MPR factions rose one by one to deliver their formal Pemandangan Umum replies, even Golkar's own spokesman slammed the speech for glossing over East Timor, Bank Bali, and the SP3 for Suharto, warning that statistics alone will not save him on October 19.

options.text: "Confront East Timor and Bank Bali with candor and humility: apologize to the nation for the shortcomings of your transitional cabinet, explain that East Timor was never recognized by the UN and had become a bleeding wound, and pledge full prosecution of anyone implicated in Bank Bali."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'PERMINTAAN MAAF DI TENGAH MALAM: KETULUSAN NEGARAWAN ATAU TAKTIK MEREDAM PALU SIDANG?'

In a dramatic departure from three decades of presidential infallibility, B.J. Habibie bowed his head from the MPR rostrum during his Jawaban Presiden reply to apologize directly to the Indonesian people for the shortcomings of his seventeen-month transition, while defending the East Timor referendum as the only way to free Indonesia from a twenty-four-year international pariah trap. The humility noticeably quieted the jeering benches of PKB and the functional groups, though nationalist hardliners in PDI-P and ABRI immediately attacked the apology as an admission of guilt that warrants rejecting his mandate.

options.text: "Deliver a fiery appeal to the Golkar family, the outer islands, and the Islamic caucus: warn the Assembly that rejecting your speech is a backdoor coup designed to erase everything ICMI, the regions, and reformist Muslims have built since May 1998."
options.reaction:
SUARA PEMBARUAN: 'PIDATO PERTANGGUNGJAWABAN RASA KAMPANYE: HABIBIE GALANG SENTIMEN KEDAERAHAN DAN ISLAM'

Dropping all pretense of a neutral constitutional accounting, President Habibie turned his three-hour address before the MPR into a combative campaign rally aimed squarely at outer-island delegates, Golkar stalwarts, and the Islamic parties of the Central Axis. While his loyalists from Sulawesi and the PBB benches cheered every line, secular nationalists and independent commentators accused the President of polarizing the chamber along regional and religious fault lines in a desperate bid to scrape together 351 votes.

options.text: "Extend a constitutional olive branch to the entire Assembly: present your 17 months as a bridge to full democracy and pledge that a 1999–2004 cabinet will be a National Unity Rainbow Cabinet shared proportionally across PDI-P, the Central Axis, Golkar, and ABRI."
options.reaction:
MEDIA INDONESIA: 'JANJI KABINET PELANGI DARI PODIUM MPR: RAYUAN TERAKHIR SEBELUM KOTAK SUARA DIBUKA'

Facing eleven factions sharpening their blades for the October 19 accountability vote, President Habibie used his address at the MPR podium to dangle the ultimate prize before every party boss in the hall: a proportional 'National Unity Rainbow Cabinet' where PDI-P, Poros Tengah, Golkar, and the military all get a slice of executive power if his speech is accepted. In the Senayan coffee lounges afterward, opposition MPs smiled cynically: 'Why take a slice of Habibie's rainbow cake when we can reject his speech tomorrow and take the whole bakery?'

title: Night of the Long Knives
desc: It is the night of October 18, 1999, less than twenty-four hours before the MPR votes by secret ballot to accept or reject your Accountability Speech. Across the eleven MPR factions, four have announced they will accept (Reformasi/PAN-PK, PBB, PDU, and FKKI), four have announced they will reject (PDI-P, PKB, KKI, and PDKB), leaving the entire survival of your presidency hanging on three decisive blocs: Golkar (120 seats), PPP (58 seats), and ABRI (38 seats), alongside the 200 regional and functional delegates. Then, two earthquakes strike within hours of each other: at 3:30 PM today, General Wiranto appeared on television to announce that after consulting the officer corps, he is declining your offer to run as your Vice Presidential candidate; and tonight at the Hotel Mulia, a rebel faction of roughly 40 Golkar delegates led by Akbar Tandjung and Marzuki Darusman ('Golkar Putih') is threatening to defect and vote 'Reject' tomorrow on secret ballot unless you pull their votes back into line at Patra Kuningan tonight.

options.text: "Summon Akbar Tandjung, Marzuki Darusman, and the entire Golkar MPR caucus to Patra Kuningan tonight: confront the 'Golkar Putih' defectors face-to-face and demand party discipline under the Banyan Tree for tomorrow's secret ballot."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'MALAM JAHANAM DI PATRA KUNINGAN: HABIBIE BENTAK AKBAR TANDJUNG DI DEPAN KADER GOLKAR'

Tempers exploded past midnight at President Habibie's private residence on Jalan Patra Kuningan as the President and A.A. Baramuli confronted Golkar Chairman Akbar Tandjung and Marzuki Darusman over reports that up to forty 'Golkar Putih' legislators intend to stab Habibie in the back during tomorrow's secret-ballot vote. Witnesses say shouting echoed into the courtyard as Sulawesi loyalists accused Akbar of treason; while Akbar emerged at 2:00 AM promising reporters that 'Golkar's official line remains to accept the speech,' nobody in Jakarta is sure what his lieutenants will actually mark once they step behind the curtain tomorrow.

options.text: "Pivot immediately after Wiranto's refusal: invite Amien Rais, Hamzah Haz, and Yusril Ihza Mahendra to Patra Kuningan and offer the Vice Presidency directly to the Central Axis and PPP in exchange for their undivided vote tomorrow."
options.reaction:
REPUBLIKA: 'DITINGGAL WIRANTO SORE HARI, MALAM HARI HABIBIE TAWARKAN KURSI WAPRES KE POROS TENGAH'

Reeling from General Wiranto's 3:30 PM televised announcement declining to run as his Vice President, President Habibie pivoted in sheer desperation last night, summoning PPP Chairman Hamzah Haz and Central Axis leaders to Patra Kuningan to offer them the vacant number-two slot before tomorrow's vote. While PPP's 58 delegates and Yusril Ihza Mahendra's PBB welcomed the late-night courtship, critics mocked the spectacle of a sitting President peddling the Vice Presidency from door to door at midnight like a last-minute concert ticket.

options.text: "Deploy A.A. Baramuli, Fadel Muhammad, and your floor whips across the hotel suites of the 135 Utusan Daerah and 65 Utusan Golongan delegates tonight to lock down every uncommitted regional and functional vote."
options.reaction:
RAKYAT MERDEKA: 'OPERASI FAJAR DI HOTEL MULIA DAN HILTON! BROKER ISTANA GERILYA BELI SUARA UTUSAN DAERAH'

Sleep was impossible inside the Hilton, Mulia, and Atlet Century Park hotels last night as operatives from President Habibie's Tim Sukses, led by A.A. Baramuli and Fadel Muhammad, went suite to suite knocking on the doors of outer-island and functional delegates ahead of today's secret ballot. Student monitors from Forum Kota camped in the hotel lobbies accused the Palace brokers of carrying briefcases of cash and project pledges to buy the 351-vote threshold before sunrise.

options.text: "Hold an urgent one-on-one meeting with General Wiranto and the ABRI faction leadership under Lt. Gen. Hari Sabarno to ensure that even though Wiranto declined the VP slot, ABRI's 38 delegates vote 'Accept' on your Accountability Speech."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'WIRANTO TOLAK PINANGAN WAPRES, FRAKSI TNI/POLRI JADI KUNCI PENENTU NASIB HABIBIE HARI INI'

General Wiranto's dramatic afternoon press conference declining President Habibie's Vice Presidential offer stunned the Patra Kuningan camp, forcing Habibie into an urgent midnight meeting with Wiranto and ABRI Faction Chairman Lt. Gen. Hari Sabarno. While the generals assured the President that stepping back from the ticket was merely to keep the armed forces neutral and that the 38-seat military bloc will 'respect constitutional continuity' today, Senayan insiders note that Wiranto has carefully untied his own lifeboat from Habibie's hull just hours before the iceberg hits.

options.text: "Reject the midnight hotel horse-trading entirely: spend the evening quietly at Patra Kuningan with Ibu Ainun and your closest family, trusting the 700 delegates of the MPR to judge your 512 days on their honest merits."
options.reaction:
THE JAKARTA POST: 'AS SENAYAN BROKERS TRADE VOTES TILL DAWN, A LONELY PRESIDENT WAITS AT KUNINGAN'

While Akbar Tandjung's dissidents, Amien Rais's Central Axis, and Taufik Kiemas's operatives spent the night horse-trading furiously across the hotel suites of Senayan after General Wiranto's afternoon bombshell, President Habibie called off his floor whips and spent a quiet evening praying with his wife Ainun at Patra Kuningan. Even his fiercest critics in the press gallery admitted a grudging respect for his refusal to turn the final night into a cash auction, though in the shark tank of the 1999 MPR, a clear conscience counts for zero votes.

title: TAP MPR No. V/1999
desc:
Twenty-one years ago, in July 1978, a New Order MPR enacted Decree No. VI (TAP MPR No. VI/MPR/1978), formally incorporating the former Portuguese colony of East Timor into the Republic of Indonesia as its 27th province, an annexation the United Nations never recognized. Today, October 19, 1999, as its final act before bringing the wooden ballot boxes onto the floor to vote by secret ballot on your Accountability Speech (TAP MPR No. III/MPR/1999), the People's Consultative Assembly takes up TAP MPR No. V/MPR/1999 on the East Timor Referendum.

With remarkably little floor resistance, the Assembly formally revokes TAP MPR No. VI/1978, constitutionally recognizing the August 30 referendum result in which 78.5% of East Timorese voters chose independence, and clearing the legal path for the United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor (UNTAET) to assume authority over the territory. As MPR Speaker Amien Rais prepares to call the 700 delegates forward one by one to cast their secret ballots on your presidency, you issue your final word on the close of the East Timor chapter.

options.text: "This twenty-four-year chapter closes today with constitutional dignity rather than endless war. Indonesia's obligations under the May 5 Agreement are honorably discharged, may Indonesia and an independent Timor Lorosa'e live side by side in peace."
options.reaction:
KOMPAS: 'MPR CABUT TAP INTEGRASI TIMTIM, KINI 700 ANGGOTA DEWAN SIAP HAKIMI NASIB HABIBIE'

In a bitter historical irony, the very same MPR factions that spent the past week savaging President Habibie for 'losing the 27th province' voted unanimously this afternoon to pass TAP MPR No. V/MPR/1999, formally revoking the 1978 integration decree and letting East Timor go without a single dissenting vote. Having used East Timor to bludgeon Habibie's reputation to pieces, the 700 delegates have now washed their own hands of the territory just in time to unlock the wooden ballot boxes and pass judgment on the man who dared to hold the referendum.

options.text: "I will not pretend this was the outcome I hoped for when we offered Wide-Ranging Autonomy, but a Republic that honors the free vote of the ballot box, even when the result hurts, proves to the world and to itself that Reformasi is real."
options.reaction:
MAJALAH TEMPO: 'BABAK TERAKHIR TIMOR TIMUR DITUTUP, PALU AMIEN RAIS MEMBUKA MALAM PENENTUAN'

With the stroke of Amien Rais's gavel ratifying TAP MPR No. V/MPR/1999, twenty-four years of blood, international isolation, and broken promises in East Timor came to a formal constitutional end this afternoon in Senayan. Yet as diplomats in the gallery applauded President Habibie's parting words on democratic honor, the floor below was already clearing for the main event: the secret-ballot roll call on his Accountability Speech has begun, and every politician in the hall is ready to collect their pound of flesh.
